newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht rebounds late, market remains jittery.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht rebounds late, market remains jittery.

text.p: The Thai baht recovered against the dollar in late trade in offshore and domestic markets but dealers remained jittery in taking baht posititons after the resignation of finance minister Amnuay Viravan, brokers said.

The baht strengthened to 25.845/25.945 to the dollar late in the domestic market from 25.920/26.050 in early trade. In the offshore market, the baht was quoted at 25.000/25.400 late against 26.500/27.500 in the morning.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the midrate at 25.77 to the dollar against 25.76 on Wednesday.
"There was panic dollar buying especially by corporates following Amnuay's resignation," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Amnuay on Thursday resigned after policy conflicts between him and political rivals in the six-party government coalition.
His ally and commerce minister Narongchai Akrasanee also tendered his resignation effective June 21.
"There was also concern about baht devaluation which prompted most borrowers of foreign loans to seek safety in dollar," the dealer said.
A senior central bank official on Thursday dismissed market concern over a baht devaluation.
When asked if there would be a devaluation after Amnuay's departure, central bank assistant governor Siri Ganjarerndee told reporters: "The market is unduly panicking. There is no need to worry."
Dealers in Singapore said persistent baht demand and sustained high swap premiums helped slow the baht's fall against the dollar in the spot market.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was traded at 255/275 satangs per dollar offshore and 28/40 onshore.
Heavy domestic buying of dollars pushed the overnight interbank rate to 16-18 percent from 14-17 in the morning.
